pageCache.text:
Home
New Sixth Form Centre named for Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah
CLC has received a landmark benefaction to create the Zarith Sofiah Centre, its new Sixth Form Centre, named in honour of Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, who studied at the College for five years in the 1970s.
For FearlessFutures
We nurture fearless individuals,ready to take on the future withcuriosity, courage and compassion.
Come and visit
Explore CLC at one of our open days or on a private visit - open to anyone interested in joining in 2027 or beyond.
FearlessMinds
At Cheltenham Ladies' College, we are here to nurture fearless individuals, ready to take on the future with curiosity, courage and compassion. The world needs more than just good grades. We help our students to find the confidence to step into the world, and dare to make a difference.
Why CheltenhamLadies' College?
Because education here is about more than achievement.
It is about inquisitive minds, brave hearts and strong values. Exceptional teaching, breadth of opportunity and a supportive community encourages students to explore ideas, take intellectual risks and discover their strengths.
The result: confident young women ready for university, ready for the workplace and ready to shape the future.
The Feed
Our Admissions team is on hand to make your application process as seamless as possible. Every year we have over 150 students join College, becoming part of a vibrant, diverse and fearless community of over 820 students.
For many of our new boarders, joining Cheltenham Ladies’ College will be the first time they have left home for any considerable period. Whether coming from the UK or overseas, our house system is structured to allow new boarders to settle in quickly, with older girls supporting and nurturing younger pupils in “House families”.
For many families, being a Day pupil offers the best of both worlds. Students are fully integrated into the College community - learning, building friendships and leading alongside boarders. Wraparound care before and after school, local bus routes and occasional boarding spaces give families flexibility, whilst ensuring that students benefit from every opportunity available to them.

Public Benefit and Partnerships
Public Benefit and Partnerships
At CLC, we partner with schools, charities and communities at every level, and through our Community Links programme, pupils volunteer extensively in primary schools, care homes, animal shelters and the local Open Door project.
Not only do we have a range of programmes, initiatives and wider strategic partnerships in place, but every year we continue to introduce new opportunities for students to find the confidence to step into the world and dare to make a difference.
Cheltenham Education Partnership
As a proud member of the Cheltenham Education Partnership (CEP), we foster opportunities for young people to realise their potential and expand their horizons through collaboration with nine state and independent schools, the University of Gloucestershire and local charities and organisations.
"Working in a truly collaborative way allows us to tap into the knowledge and experience amongst the pupil and staff bodies in our town."
Mr Will Parker, CLC CEP Lead
Initiatives
Through our partnership with Teen Tips, pupils, staff and parents gain expert mental health support via The Wellbeing Hub. We extend free access to the hub to three local maintained schools, supporting over 2,000 students, parents and staff across Pittville, Balcarras and The High School Leckhampton.
We also deliver initiatives such as Laptops for Learning, swim teaching, Starlab sessions, science conferences and maths challenge events.
Schools Together
Explore more of College's larger projects and longstanding partnerships on the national Schools Together database.

pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome
A Pioneering Past,
Fearless Futures.
For nearly 175 years, we have believed that girls deserve to be at the forefront of education.
At CLC, students are empowered to ask difficult questions, have the self-confidence to think and speak independently, and strive to collaborate and take the lead with courage and compassion.
Hear from Eve Jardine-Young, Executive Principal, and Jemima Edney, Head of College, as they discuss their thoughts on what it means to be fearless.
Fearlessness is about not being afraid to make mistakes. It's about approaching every challenge with confidence, with courage, and with heart.
Jemima Edney, Head of College
Our Timeline
Since 1853, we have been nurturing and developing the next generation of fearless individuals taking on, shaping and positively impacting the world through their curiosity, courage and compassion.
Our Values
Teaching and caring for pupils from over 50 countries empowers us to think globally and celebrate diversity.
A holistic education at CLC is about developing agility to manage change, the resilience to take learn from mistakes, and the courage to meet the challenges of the future.
We encourage students to choose who they want to become, understand how to make meaningful connections, and decide what they can trust.
Pupils develop strong confidence. they eagerly and resolutely seek new challenges to stretch their boundaries and aspirations.
ISI Inspection, November 2022
Our Culture & Ethos
We develop and nurture fearless individuals with curious minds. At Cheltenham Ladies’ College we provide educational experiences that are deliberately wide and expansive, encouraging and supporting pupils to explore opportunities and possibilities, to question as well as answer, to think as well as learn, developing the curiosity and confidence to choose their own path.
At Cheltenham Ladies’ College we provide educational experiences that develop and nurture mindsets, as well as skillsets. So our pupils leave us not only with the qualifications and grades they need to succeed, but the courage to give things a go, the confidence to fail as well as succeed and the self-belief and determination to keep going.
At CLC, community is at the heart of our approach and through the many opportunities to learn and grow beyond the classroom and connect with others in school and in the broader community, students develop the compassion to want to make a difference and the confidence and determination
Our Campus & the Cotswolds
Regency Cheltenham, bordering the beautiful Cotswolds AONB, is home to CLC, our staff and our students.
With restaurants, a great range of shops, and many literary, music and arts festivals each year, it's a fantastic place to learn, relax, and grow.
Why CLC?
Which is better, single-sex or co-education?
What is boarding really like?
How can you be sure CLC is the right school?
We firmly believe that each family must make the choices that are right for them, but here's why we think a girls-only environment at CLC helps to develop curious, compassionate, and fearless individuals.
Start your Journey
Find out more

Our Strategy
OUR STRATEGY
FOR FEARLESS FUTURES
Over the past decade, schools worldwide have faced unprecedented challenges, from Covid’s lasting impact to growing financial and political pressures, yet we continue to move forward with purpose.
Our pupils remain at the heart of everything we do, and this commitment is woven through our forward‑focused strategy, strengthening our core Vision, Mission and Values in a rapidly changing world.
Entering the next decade from a position of strength, supported by the substantive commentary of the recent ISI Inspection report and a clear sense of direction, we do so with confidence, agility and intent.
Vision, Mission and Values
Our vision is to embody excellence, independence, inspiration and empowerment in the education of women.
Our mission is to support and guide girls in becoming self-determining, fulfilled and resilient women who value, serve and enrich the communities to which they belong in a complex and changing world and to honour our pioneering heritage through challenge and innovation in the pursuit of academic excellence.
Our values are to promote mutual respect, integrity, courage and the productive exchange of ideas, and to nurture intellectual curiosity, creativity, confidence and an enduring sense of belonging.
Our Strategic Aims
Embrace purposeful development and an enduring love of learning, grounded in academic rigour, ready for life beyond CLC.
Recruit and retain excellent staff and governors underpinned by strong and supportive leadership and a deep-seated sense of belonging.
Support pupils and staff in leading healthy, happy and meaningful lives, connecting positively with others and their environment.
Nurture a diverse and inclusive pupil, parent and staff community which collectively embodies the values of global citizens.
Maintain sound, ethical and responsive financial management with a focus on innovation, to meet all our strategic aims on a sustainable long-term basis.
Five Year Plan
From our pledge to carbon net zero, a renewed commitment to transformational bursaries, and the development of our new world-leading Sixth Form Centre, we continue to take an ambitious, innovative, and fearless approach to our future.
Over the next decade, we plan to continue to build our bursary endowment fund, pursue our sustainability goals, and continue to invest in appropriate major capital projects, all aligned to our strategic aims.

pageCache.pageTitle: Past & Future: The History of Cheltenham Ladies' College | CLC | Cheltenham Ladies' College
pageCache.text:
Past and Future
Past and Future
CLC first opened its doors because our founders believed their daughters deserved a better education.
In the 1800s, despite opposition, we introduced science, mechanics and hydrostatics. In WWI, students ran a Red Cross branch and a hospital, and during WWII, we sent female pioneers to Bletchley Park.
In the late 1900s, we invested in opportunities within science and traditionally male-dominated sports, and introduced computer studies and car maintenance.
Since 2000, we have championed better approaches to women's health, fitness, and wellbeing, and introduced engineering and psychology.
CLC has been a pioneer in girls' education for nearly 175 years.
We're just getting started.
Our Timeline
In 1865, we introduced science, mechanics and hydrostatics, despite opposition that these subjects were not 'ladylike'.
Our Principal founded St Hilda’s College at Oxford University, firm in her belief that women should have access to higher education.
During WWI, we ran a branch of the Red Cross branch and a VAD hospital. Students also grew and harvested food across the playing fields.
In the 1930s, we were the first girls’ school to receive a Royal Charter in over 200 years.
During WWII, we were determined to continue to educating girls. With all other building given over to the war effort, we boarded the swimming pool and turned changing cubicles into study spaces.
From the 1950 to the 60s, we invested in a new science wing, and introduced a range of traditionally male-dominated sports, like Golf, Archery, Orienteering, Sailing, and Canoeing.
In the 1970 and 80s, we opened a new Sixth Form Block, and introduced computer studies and car maintenance lessons.
In the 90s and 2000s, we opened a new sports hall and built a new art wing, theatre and performing arts centre, and welcomed Queen Elizabeth II to celebrate our 150th Anniversary.
From 2010 to 2020, we invested in health and wellbeing, building a state-of-the-art new Health & Fitness Centre, and a bespoke Wellbeing Programme.
We also added Engineering, Enterprise and Technology, and Psychology to the curriculum.
Our Future
We continue to take an ambitious, innovative, and fearless approach to our future.
From our pledge to aim for carbon net zero, a renewed commitment to transformational bursaries, and the development of our new world-leading Sixth Form Centre.
Archives
CLC has a fascinating and inspiring history, dating back to when the school was founded. Our incredible collections are maintained and catalogued by our Archive Department.
We have an outstanding collection of treasures, gathered by CLC girls and staff over more than 170 years. Our Archive contains about 4,500 books, thousands of photographs and examples of clothing and teaching equipment from the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries.
If you have an enquiry relating to the history of CLC, you are invited to send your request to our Archivist. We receive many enquiries and although we will try, we cannot always answer immediately as it can sometimes take time to carry out the necessary research.
In our enquiries, it helps to have as much background information as possible. This is especially the case if it is information about someone who might have been at CLC, in which case details such as date of birth, alternative / maiden name (if applicable) and why you think they might have been at College, are all useful when trying to trace a particular name. Please include your email address and telephone number and we will contact you as soon as possible.
If you are a parent, pupil or Guild member, this service is free. Otherwise, if the search is successful, we ask for a fee of £10.00 to cover costs, including photocopies of documents if relevant. If we are unsuccessful, we will let you know and there is no fee.

pageCache.text:
Why CLC?
Why CLC?
Cheltenham Ladies’ College has been at the forefront of girls’ education for over 170 years.
Our global reputation was founded on our pioneering approach to girls’ education and our future aims are no less ambitious.
For Fearless Futures
The world needs more than just good grades.
It needs inquisitive minds, brave hearts and strong values.
At Cheltenham Ladies’ College, we are here to nurture fearless individuals, ready to take on the future with curiosity, courage and compassion.
That's why we empower whilst we educate. We develop mindsets alongside skillsets. We teach students to think, as well as learn. To question, not just answer. To succeed, whilst learning to fail. Working in communities, not just classrooms.
We help every student experience the joy of learning, find the confidence to step into the world and dare to make a difference.
CLC is the Top Girls Boarding School in the World for the IB (Education Advisers League Table 2026)
CLC has been named Top Independent School in the South West for Academic Performance for the last 5 years - Parent Power (The Sunday Times)
CLC is ranked in the top 10 schools in the world for IB results (Education Advisers League Table 2026)
CLC was named South West Independent Secondary School of the Decade in 2021 by The Sunday Times
CLC has been ranked in the Top 100 Independent Schools in the World for the last 5 years - Spear's Schools Index 2026
Why All Girls?
There are many arguments surrounding the benefits and disadvantages of single-sex vs co-educational schools. Ultimately, each child’s education should be right for them, with teaching that inspires them, debates that challenge them and opportunities that allow them to thrive.
Our approach to education has always been to put girls first.
We believe that our pupils thrive in a single-sex environment. They develop resilience and confidence in a culture that encourages them to believe that nothing is beyond their reach.
The success of this approach is demonstrated not only in their consistently outstanding exam results and extensive co-curricular achievements, but through the well-rounded and inspirational women they become.
Whether a budding scientist, inspired artist or talented sportswoman, we encourage them to develop independent thought, and to support and challenge each other.
Why Boarding?
We have a fantastic and strong community of Day and Boarding students.
Surrounded by the fictional worlds of Malory Towers, Harry Potter and St Trinian’s, there are many far-reaching myths about boarding.
We know that for some families boarding for the first time can feel really daunting.
In reality, modern boarding offers the opportunity for girls to be immersed in a supportive, vibrant, and diverse community of peers and friends, where they can express themselves and debate their views, grow and learn together, and develop lifelong friendships.
Modern technology ensures family and friends are only a message or video call away and our pastoral support, between school and the boarding houses, is designed to nurture and encourage students to settle quickly.
From eating meals or watching a film together, to rehearsing for House Music or working on a group entry for the Upcycled Fashion Show, boarding houses quickly become a home from home.

Inspection Reports
Inspection Reports
The Independent Schools Inspectorate is appointed by the Department of Education to inspect association independent schools in England. Their inspections report on the extent to which the statutory Independent School Standards and other applicable regulatory requirements are met, collectively referred to in the reports as ‘the Standards’.
Leadership and management, and governance
Quality of education, training and recreation
Pupils’ physical and mental health and emotional wellbeing
Pupils’ social and economic education and contribution to society
Inspection Report 2026
College underwent an inspection in December 2025, and was found to be fully compliant in all areas.
In addition, College received a Significant Strength, given in recognition of its co-ordination of curricular, co-curricular and pastoral care programmes and the contribution this makes to pupils’ development.

pageCache.text:
Academic Scholars
Academic Scholars
Inquisitive Minds
Academic Scholars at Cheltenham Ladies’ College are driven by curiosity - a desire to question, explore and understand the world in greater depth.
We encourage and support our scholars to explore opportunities and possibilities that are deliberately wide and expansive. We encourage them to question as well as answer and to think as well as learn.
Our Academic Scholars’ Programme is designed to extend learning beyond the classroom, creating space for ideas, discussion and intellectual risk-taking.
Learning Beyond the Curriculum
Scholars are encouraged to go further: to look beyond the specification, challenge assumptions and engage with complex, real-world questions.
Through a programme of extension, discussion and independent enquiry, students develop the confidence to think for themselves, and to articulate their ideas with clarity.
Our Academic Scholars are active contributors to College life - inside and outside the classroom. They lead discussions and support others, bringing energy, insight and challenge.
Our Academic Scholars play a key role in the life of College and have access to a wealth of opportunities designed to enrich, inspire and challenge them to think critically
Dr David Gamblin, Vice Principal Academic
Forum 42
Our Forum42 Society offers opportunities and enrichment to stretch and inspire our pupils. The number 42 pays homage to Douglas Adams’ The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy in which it is the answer given by a supercomputer to “the Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything”.
Internal peer-to-peer TEDx style talks on topics as varied as 'The History of Rugby' to 'Can Science disprove free will?' are complimented by external talks from wide-ranging speakers. We have recently welcomed the Head of an Oxbridge College, an aerodynamicist, the first female three-star RAF officer, the founder of a gospel music festival and a theologist.

Pastoral Care
Pastoral Care
Supporting Our Students
At CLC, each student is nurtured, supported and empowered to develop their hopes and ambitions for life beyond CLC. We recognise that adolescence is challenging, so we provide a secure and supportive community where pupils can flourish and gain the confidence, skills and resilience needed to lead happy, healthy and purposeful lives.
We want to ensure that every student at College feels supported, happy and fulfilled during their time with us. Life isn’t without challenges, but having people alongside you to help you face those ups and downs is really, really important.
Miss Caroline Ralph, Head of Pastoral Care
We handle sensitive issues with care, encouraging pupils to express their views and discuss challenging topics at a pace that feels comfortable.
Pupils have access to trained peer support, school counsellors, specialist staff and, when appropriate, external professionals.
We celebrate the positive moments through sport, creative arts and community activities across Houses and College, ensuring pupils have space to enjoy fun, connection and laughter simply for the joy of it.

Bursaries
Bursaries
Fearless Futures start with opening up opportunities
Means-tested bursaries, known as Beale Awards, enable young women to pursue educational experiences, no matter their financial background.
Beale Awards offer fully or partially funded boarding or day places at College - from 1%-100%, depending on circumstances. Around 65 pupils receive fees support via a Beale Award, totaling approximately £1.6million annually.
We are now accepting day and boarding applications for entry in 2027 to Year 7 and Year 12 (Sixth Form) - please see below for more details on the application process.
Please complete an Enquiry Form so we can keep in touch with further details as they become available.
Without my Beale Award, my life would be far less rich than it is now. CLC opened my eyes to new cultures, new opportunities, and has really shaped me into the woman that I am today.
Gracie, Former pupil and Beale Award recipient
Common Questions
We are currently welcoming bursary applications for 2027 for LC1 (Year 7/11+) Day & Boarding and Sixth Form (16+) Day & Boarding. Applicant families must be UK taxpayers. Please see the Key Dates and application process below.
If you are considering applying for a Beale Award, please complete our Beale Award Enquiry Form well in advance of the point that you are looking to join.
This will give our team the initial information they need to support you through your Beale Award application and give you the greatest chance of being considered for the funds available.
Applications are accepted from families where the fee-paying parent(s) are resident in the UK for tax purposes.
After an initial conversation with our Admissions Team, families interested in applying for a Beale Award will be asked to complete our Beale Award Registration Form through our Admission Portal.
There is a £12 fee to pay at the point you initially register, and subsequent admissions/acceptance fees and deposits will be pro-rated in line with any financial award offered. More details are available in our fees section. If you are not offered a place at College as part of the Beale Award process then the registration fee of £12 will be fully refunded to the original payment source.
The Admissions Team will guide you through the rest of the process. The percentage of fees support provided is determined through our financial means-testing process. Awards granted consider both your financial circumstances and your daughter's performance in her written entrance tests and interviews.
Joining CLC in Year 7? Get in touch during Year 5.
Joining CLC in Year 12? Get in touch during Year 10.
Beale Awards are available for day and boarding students joining Year 7 in 2027.
Deadline to register – mid-September 2026
Assessments - first two weeks of October 2026
Applicants will complete a financial review following the results of the assessments in October 2026
Final outcome will be communicated in January 2027
Beale Awards are available for those joining at Year 12 in 2026 as either a day student or a boarder.
Deadline to register – end of September 2026
Assessments - Early November 2026
Applicants will complete a financial review following the results of the assessments in December 2026
Final outcome will be communicated in January 2027
CLC offers an enriching Scholarship Programme with a wealth of opportunities aimed at stretching and developing individual talent for the benefit of the whole community.
Scholarship Awards do not carry fee remission but families can apply for assistance with fees through the Beale Award scheme.
All financial awards are means tested and include pro-rated assistance towards the additional costs of attending, including uniform and co-curricular activities. For the full list of extras and details of inclusions, please request a copy of the Bursary Extras document from the Admissions Department.
The percentage award your daughter has been offered will be reviewed annually as part of the College’s normal financial review processes which ensure that support continues to be allocated fairly and responsibly.
Where a family’s financial circumstances remain broadly the same, the level of support would normally be expected to continue at a similar level. If circumstances change, the level of support may increase or decrease, and should your circumstances change mid-year we encourage you to contact us so we can discuss what interim support may be available.
For full guidance, please request a copy of our Bursaries Policy from our Admissions team.
Over the years we have supported a number of military families through means-tested bursaries.
CLC do not offer a set reduction in fees for military families, instead, we recommend you apply for a Beale Award.
We only accept applications from families who are UK tax payers.
For more details on means-tested bursaries, please request a copy of our Bursaries Policy and Procedure and Bursary Extras from the Admissions Department.

pageCache.pageTitle: Become a Scholar | Cheltenham Ladies' College
pageCache.text:
Scholarships
Scholarships
Recognising potential -Rewarding excellence
Scholarships at Cheltenham Ladies’ College are designed to recognise students with exceptional ability, curiosity and commitment.
Awarded at 11+, 13+ and 16+ entry, scholarships celebrate strengths and talents across a range of disciplines. They also reflect a willingness to engage fully in College life, to contribute, and to make the most of the opportunities available.
Become a scholar
Available at 11+, 13+ and 16+
Academic Scholars are curious, thoughtful and ambitious. Our bespoke programme supports their intellectual, cultural and personal development, encouraging them to think independently and explore ideas in depth.
At 11+ and 13+, all applicants are considered, with selected candidates invited to further assessment.
At 16+, students apply directly on their Entrance Exam Form and shortlisted candidates attend an assessment day in November of Year 11.
Please note the deadline to apply for 16+ 2027 Academic Scholarships has now passed.
Available at 13+ and 16+
Art Scholarships recognise creativity, curiosity and passion across a range of media.
Scholars exhibit their work regularly and engage with galleries, exhibitions and visiting speakers. Many continue their artistic journey beyond College.
Assessment includes a portfolio and practical task. (There are no Art Scholarships at 11+, but opportunities are available to apply for internal scholarships at the end of Lower College.)
Please note the deadline to apply for 16+ 2027 Art Scholarships has now passed.
Our Drama Scholarships recognise creativity, commitment, enthusiasm and talent across a range of dramatic disciplines, including acting, design and theatre-making, and scholars are expected to play a leading role in CLC productions throughout their time at College. Scholars benefit from an extensive programme of productions, workshops, performances, live theatre visits and sessions with visiting practitioners, helping them develop skills both on stage and behind the scenes and supporting progression to Drama-related university or drama school courses.
Applications are considered at 13+ and 16+, with shortlisted candidates taking part in a practical audition and interview that includes performance and discussion of their interest in Drama.
Please note the deadline to apply for 16+ 2027 Drama Scholarships has now passed.
Available at 11+, 13+ and 16+
Music Scholars bring energy, discipline and a genuine love of music. They display a natural musicianship and play a central role in ensembles and performances across College.
Assessment includes performance, aural tests and interview. While there is no formal minimum standard, most successful candidates are working at the following ABRSM levels in their principal study:
11+/Year 7: Grade 4 +
13+/Year 9: Grade 5 +
16+/Sixth Form: Grade 7 +
Please note the deadline to apply for 16+ 2027 Music Scholarships has now passed.
A distinctive opportunity for promising organists. Candidates should have Grade 6+ keyboard skills, preferably with confident sight-reading ability, and previous experience playing or studying the organ.
Organ Scholars follow a specialist programme, working closely with the College Organist and contributing to College music. The role offers extensive performance opportunities and preparation for university-level study.
Please note the deadline to apply for 16+ 2027 Organ Scholarships has now passed.
Available at 13+ and 16+
Sports Scholars lead with commitment and integrity, representing College across multiple teams and often playing at county level or beyond.
They are supported by expert coaching and play an active role in mentoring younger students. Assessment includes practical performance and interview.
(There are no Sport Scholarships at 11+, but opportunities to develop are supported in the early years and there are opportunities to apply for internal scholarships at the end of Lower College.)
Please note the deadline to apply for 16+ 2027 Sport Scholarships has now passed.
There is no cookie‑cutter perfect scholar… as long as you’re authentic and have a passion and drive to learn, that’s what really matters.”
Helena - Sixth Form Academic Scholar
Ongoing support
Becoming a Scholar at CLC is the beginning of a journey.
Scholars benefit from an enriched programme designed to stretch, challenge and inspire - encouraging them to think independently, explore ideas in greater depth and engage with the world around them.
Financial Support
Scholarships recognise excellence but do not provide means-tested financial support.
If you require a place with financial support, this is available via the Beale Awards, our bursary programme. A Beale Award is means-tested and offers up to 100% fee remission for families who require financial assistance. Beale Awards are available for entry in Year 7 or Year 12 (both day and boarding). Applicant families must be UK taxpayers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Support for Sudden School Closures | Cheltenham Ladies' College
pageCache.text:
Support for Sudden School Closures
Support for Sudden School Closures
Here to help when plans change
We understand that an unexpected school closure can be an unsettling time for girls and their families, particularly when decisions about education have to be made at short notice.
If your daughter is affected, we would be pleased to talk with you about her circumstances and the options available at CLC. Our Admissions and Academic teams can explain the process, compare academic courses and, where a suitable place is available, help you understand what a move to CLC could look like.
How we can support you
Contact us to arrange a 1-2-1 call with a member of the Admissions team or the relevant Head of Division to discuss your daughter’s position and what we may be able to do to support.
For pupils about to enter Year 11 or Year 13, we understand that this might be a particularly worrying time, as you consider how your daughter can continue her education as seamlessly as possible. We will look at your daughter’s GCSE or A Level pathway and consider how we might be able to support her. If you would like to make an appointment for a discussion, please email admissions@cheltladiescollege.org.
Attend our next Open Event to meet key members of staff (Academic, Pastoral, Day, Boarding and Co-curricular), tour the campus and Houses and speak directly with the Admissions team about possible next steps.
Common Questions
Contact our Admissions team so we can arrange a discussion with our Admissions Director, Mr Richard Houchin, and relevant members of the Academic team.
In the first instance, we recommend you contact our Admissions team for a discussion so that we can understand your individual situation. We can then ensure that we have the relevant members of Academic staff on hand to address concerns and queries, and confirm any admissions requirements.
We are looking to make any transition as seamless and easy to navigate as possible. Each application will be treated with the care and detail it deserves.
As a starting point, it would be useful to have the last two reports your daughter has received, as well as any baseline data/testing outcomes (such as ALIS/MidYIS/Yellis) to hand.
Please do contact us at each year point, and we will discuss that with you during our online or in-person meeting.
CLC prides itself on its inclusive and friendly community and we hope that, if you are able to visit us, you and your daughter will be reassured by meeting our pupils and staff. If a face-to-face visit is not possible, we are happy to arrange online meetings with relevant members of the team.
We have an extensive pastoral support network in place and regularly welcome pupils across all year groups at different points of the school year.
A good starting point is to explore our website to get more of a sense of life at CLC.
Scholarships are honorary and carry no financial reward. However, we would look, where appropriate to award these highly prestigious accolades to deserving applicants.
CLC prides itself on supporting families and pupils by way of means-tested Bursaries named in honour of former Principal, Dorothea Beale. If you are presently in receipt of means-tested support, please contact us to discuss further.

The CLC Experience
THE CLC EXPERIENCE
Over the Easter and Summer holidays, Cheltenham Ladies' College will welcome a small group of girls aged 9–11 to experience a gentle introduction to life at one of the UK’s leading independent schools.
Over four nights and five days, participants will enjoy a carefully designed mix of academic tasters, creative and sporting activities, and a day trip to a local wildlife park — all while staying in one of our friendly College boarding houses with 24-hour supervision.
Easter Dates: Monday 5th April to Friday 9th April 2027
Summer Dates: Monday 19th July to Friday 23rd July 2027
Age Group: For girls currently in Year 5 or Year 6 with an independent - advanced level of English (aged 9–11)
Fees: £1,550 (includes full board, tuition, activities and excursions)
Non-residential places available on request
[My daughter] hasn't stopped talking about her wonderful time at CLC! Through our chats, I know she thoroughly enjoyed every single activity and has returned with so many lovely memories.
Parent of CLC Experience 2026 Attendee
What's Included
Engaging morning sessions across a range of subjects, taught by CLC teachers
Fun, hands-on sessions that build confidence, teamwork, and curiosity
An off-site trip to explore and share new experiences
Live and learn in one of our welcoming boarding houses, supported by experienced House staff
Round-the-clock supervision and a caring environment where every girl feels at home
A chance to explore the beautiful and historic site of Cheltenham Ladies’ College, plus an opportunity to discover more of the town in your spare time
BOOK A PLACE
If you have any questions regarding the programme, please feel free to get in touch.
Email: venuesandevents@cheltladiescollege.org

pageCache.pageTitle: Become a UK boarder | Cheltenham Ladies' College
pageCache.text:
UK Boarders
UK boarding
A place to grow, belong and make a difference
Choosing boarding at Cheltenham Ladies’ College is about more than where your daughter will live and learn. It’s about the kind of person she will become.
Each year, around 160 students join a diverse and vibrant community of approximately 850 pupils, the majority of whom board. Together, they form a community shaped by curiosity, courage and compassion.
CLC students are encouraged to think deeply, act with integrity and develop the confidence to make a positive impact - within College and beyond.
A balanced and supportive environment
Boarding life at CLC is carefully designed to support the achievement and wellbeing of each individual. Our boarding houses are more than places to stay - they are communities where students feel known, supported and encouraged to be themselves.
Evenings and weekends bring opportunities to explore new interests, spend time with friends and take part in a wide-ranging programme of activities, from creative workshops and performances to trips and outdoor adventures.
It is often in these moments that confidence grows, friendships deepen and students discover new passions.
Home-from-home boarding houses offering time and space to rest, reflect and build friendships.
Challenging, forward-thinking academics with a focus on collaborative learning and innovation.
A broad co-curricular programme of sport, the arts, humanities, leadership opportunities, community work and volunteering.
"The school has a clear focus on supporting the emotional wellbeing of boarding and day pupils, both inside and outside the classroom" ISI 2026
A strong focus on wellbeing and a culture of kindness, inclusion and mutual respect.
Flexibility for UK families
Boarding at CLC aims to work in partnership with family life.
As a full boarding school with a thriving weekend activity programme, there is never a shortage of things going on. On many weekends, there is also the option for students to go home most term time weekends after their Saturday commitments, returning in time for supper on Sunday evening.
We also support families with:
Organised transport routes to London, Oxford, the Midlands and the North.
Escorted airport transfers at the start and end of term.
A shuttle service to Cheltenham Spa station.
The result is a boarding experience that feels both independent and connected.
At Exeat weekends, half terms and the end of terms, we offer chaperoned transport routes across the UK, and escorted airport transfers at the start and end of term.
We also run a shuttle service to Cheltenham Spa station to meet the most popular London-bound train for Exeats and half terms.
Key entry points
A warm and supportive start to senior school. Students join our Junior Houses and quickly become part of a nurturing community that builds confidence, curiosity and independence.
Join our vibrant and diverse Upper College cohort, and begin shaping the GCSE journey with a strong sense of purpose and belonging.
Join our Sixth Form to study A Levels or the IB, developing independence, and build confidence and leadership skills whilst forging a path for your future.
Occasional places may become available in other year groups. Our Admissions team will be happy to advise on availability.
Common Questions
CLC is a full boarding school. Students live in boarding houses during term time, returning home for exeat weekends and holidays. We also offer day places.
As a full boarding school with a thriving weekend activity programme, there is never a shortage of things going on. However, we understand that every family is different and have varying needs outside of College, so there is also an option for students to go home on most term-time weekends after their Saturday commitments, returning in time for supper on Sunday evening.
All applicants sit entrance assessments. Requirements and timelines vary by entry year group. Full details are available in our entry guides.
Where possible, yes. Changes are usually made at the start of an academic year, but we will always try to accommodate individual circumstances.
Yes. Scholarships are available at most entry points, whilst others are available for current students to apply for.
Means-tested bursaries (covering up to 100% of fees) are offered at 11+ and 16+. We encourage early application to ensure your application is considered.

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic Subjects | Cheltenham Ladies' College | Cheltenham Ladies' College
pageCache.text:
Departments
Departments
CHOICE, DEPTH AND OPPORTUNITY
Academic departments at College combine strong results with a wide range of enriching lessons and activities. Students benefit from a broad education from LC1 (Year 7) to SFC2 (Year 13), studying more than 30 subjects, alongside conferences, clubs and trips that extend learning beyond the classroom.
Students take GCSEs or IGCSEs in UC4 and UC5 (Years 10–11), before choosing either A Levels or the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme in the Sixth Form. Unlike many schools, there are no fixed option blocks - instead, students are guided to choose subjects that suit their interests, with the timetable built around them.
The Art department is based in the Fauconberg Wing, with dedicated studio spaces, a large printmaking studio, textiles equipment, an art library and a traditional photography darkroom.
Studios remain open after school, giving pupils time and space to develop their work independently and make full use of specialist facilities. A programme of clubs and workshops - including Photography Club, LC Art Club and Life Drawing (SFC) - supports them further.
Biology at Cheltenham explores life at every scale, from whole ecosystems to the molecular processes that sustain them. Students are encouraged to question, investigate and develop a deeper understanding of the natural world through both practical and theoretical study.
Teaching takes place in six well-equipped laboratories, supported by experienced technicians.
Girls are exposed to the amazing variety of substances that make up our world in Chemistry classes. They appreciate why they are the way they are, why they behave as they do and how they can be adapted and exploited in modern life.
Girls will explore a body of chemical theories and facts, which enable them to identify patterns and themes fundamental to chemistry.
Classics invites students to explore the ancient world through its texts, ideas and material culture.
Working with sources in both the original language and in translation, students learn to analyse, interpret and question what they read.
Students follow a programme that covers both digital literacy and computer science. In the latter, an emphasis is put on algorithmic or computational thinking.
We teach girls to design and create code themselves, but we also give them the skills and understanding to solve problems in a wider context.
Based in the stunning Parabola Arts Centre, the Drama Department not only benefits from a beautiful 325-seat theatre but also a large number of rehearsal rooms. These are used for academic lessons,and for LAMDA and Trinity Speech and Drama classes.
In the main College building we also have a black box studio theatre, which is fully equipped with lighting and sound.
The great economist Milton Friedman said that societies run on greed, great achievements of civilisation do not happen at Government desks, and free enterprise is the best way to improve the lives of ordinary people.
By the end of A Level Economics at College, girls will have an opinion on whether he was right, as well as many other important discussions in the news today.
Engineering, Enterprise and Technology is taught through project-based, hands-on learning. Students design, test and refine ideas, developing practical skills alongside an understanding of how technology works in real-world contexts.
In English, students explore a wide range of voices, texts and perspectives. We recognise and value the diversity of experiences students bring with them, alongside the many forms of English they speak and encounter.
Reading is both broad and purposeful, supported by the development of clear, thoughtful writing. Students learn to construct and refine their ideas through discussion, feedback and independent work, building confidence in both analysis and expression.
Food and nutrition aims to equip students with the knowledge, understanding and skills to cook and apply the principles of food science, nutrition and healthy eating.
Students learn a range of practical skills whilst preparing and cooking nutritious dishes. The knowledge and skills gained will enable them to feed themselves and others affordably and nutritiously, now and later in life.
Geography is the study of the Earth’s landscapes, peoples, places and environments. It is, quite simply, about the world in which we live.
Geography is taught with an emphasis on making the subject dynamic, contemporary and relevant. At the heart of studying Geography in College is the desire to find out more about why, and how, elements of the world work.
At Cheltenham Ladies’ College, we believe History is not a static record preserved in textbooks, but a dynamic and evolving dialogue between past and present.
Our very surroundings offer daily reminders of how history continues to shape the world we live in. Studying History here means learning to question, to analyse, and to challenge accepted narratives with academic rigour and an open mind.
Lessons in History of Art begin with close study of works of art and architecture, using visual analysis to develop understanding and discussion. Students learn how to look carefully, interpret meaning and place works within their historical and cultural context.
Taught at Sixth Form level, the subject does not require prior experience and does not involve practical work. It complements a wide range of subjects, from the humanities to the sciences, offering a broader perspective on visual and cultural understanding.
Mathematics contributes to the school curriculum by developing pupils’ abilities to calculate; to reason logically, algebraically, and geometrically; to solve problems and to handle data.
As a subject in its own right, Mathematics presents frequent opportunities for creativity, and can stimulate moments of pleasure and wonder when a problem is solved for the first time.
Modern Languages is a broad and interdisciplinary subject, spanning language, literature, film, history and politics. Through learning to speak, write, listen and read in other languages, students develop flexible thinking and a deeper understanding of the world around them.
At CLC, the department is one of the largest in the UK. Core languages include Mandarin Chinese, French, Italian, German and Spanish, with Japanese offered in the Sixth Form. We also support students’ home and additional languages wherever possible, including Modern Greek and Russian.
College has a long and proud history of music-making. Its former Directors of Music include the composers Herbert Sumsion and John Sanders, and Music has always formed a vital filament running through the day-to-day life of many College girls.
Today, it continues to lie at the very heart of our community. Around 50 specialist and highly qualified staff teach over 1,200 individual lessons and groups each week.
From the earliest lessons in Lower College, girls will find topics are always related to the world around them. Pupils thrive when they can see the real-life relevance of a subject.
Problem solving is an innate aspect of physics, so students always need to be ready to think on their feet and voice their opinions and ideas.
Studying Politics at A Level helps students understand how power and decision-making shape society - locally, nationally, and globally. It develops critical thinking, debate, and analytical skills that are valuable for university and beyond. In today’s world of rapid political change and global challenges, Politics is more relevant than ever, equipping students to engage thoughtfully with the issues that define our future.
Psychology is a scientific discipline that looks at how human biology, family and environmental factors inter-play in determining our behaviour. Students will gain insight into the mind, brain and human behaviour as well as learning about the history of this multi-faceted subject.
With increasing awareness of the importance of psychological and mental health, there has never been a more important time to study Psychology.
We have put together an exciting programme of study that we believe gives pupils a more nuanced understanding of the beliefs and ideas held across the world, as well as the ability to evaluate critically these ideas for themselves.
From Plato’s Cave to the Pillars of Islam, from the Buddhist Noble Eightfold Path to Social Contract Theory, from Hindu views of reincarnation to Plato’s approach to reality, pupils will be given the opportunity to encounter and engage with some of the most important ideas that have influenced the way humanity lives and thinks.
Physical Education is compulsory for all year groups and plays a major part in the life of College. Our programme gives every pupil an understanding and value of the importance of physical activity in her daily life. At the heart of what we do is creating confident and competent learners through excellent teaching.
We are only a part of each girl’s journey, whether she is a regular gym user, recreational jogger or international athlete. We aim for all pupils to be consistently active for their own reasons and we support them to flourish in their chosen sports or activities.
At CLC, we view Personal, Social, Health and Economic education (PSHE) as a way to support our pupils to become healthy, safe, confident people, well prepared for the challenges and decisions they will face.
The curriculum addresses a wide range of pressing issues facing young people today, including relationships, mental and physical health, staying safe online, financial literacy, and future careers.
Research shows that students who complete an Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) are often better prepared for university, with many institutions making alternative offers to applicants who have undertaken one.
ACADEMIC SUPPORT
Our dedicated Professional Guidance Centre (PGC) offers a wealth of insight, expertise and opportunity to help encourage, guide, support and embolden pupils as they strive to find the right path for them.
Our students visit the PGC from their very earliest days in College, enabling them to make informed choices at key times during their school life. This approach promotes independence, nurtures confidence and encourages the girls to feel excited about what lies ahead.
The Learning Support Department offers tailored provision for pupils with a range of learning needs. Support programmes are reviewed regularly to track progress and ensure they remain focused on individual needs.
Our aim is to help all pupils thrive by recognising their individual learning profiles and supporting them in developing the skills they need to succeed.
There are two libraries at College - the Main Library, which holds more than 23,000 books and provides a range of spaces for private study, and the Lower College Library, which offers a 9,000‑item collection tailored to younger learners. Together, their traditional environments and extensive print collections are complemented by modern facilities and a wide range of digital resources.

Results and Beyond
Results & Beyond
At CLC, girls thrive in the classroom and far beyond it.
Our educational ethos encourages and supports students to go beyond their comfort zone, to challenge themselves academically and intellectually, and develop the courage to give things a go.
CLC offers an expansive curriculum, strong academic enrichment and many opportunities for leadership roles. As such, students go onto diverse courses in some of the best universities in the UK, US and around the world, as well as varied careers and fulfilling lives.
Exam Results
Our consistently excellent GCSE, A Level and IB Diploma results reflect the hard work of our students and teachers. We are incredibly proud of them.
IB Results 2026
Read more about our most recent results in our latest news article.
A Level Results 2026
Read more about our most recent results in our latest news article.
GCSE / IGCSE Results 2026
Read more about our most recent results in our latest news article.
Beyond CLC
Students go on to universities across the world, from top UK institutions and US Colleges, to Europe, Asia and Australia.
On leaving CLC, our alumnae become members of Guild.
Guild is our global network made up of thousands of former students, ranging from 18 to over 100 years old, who regularly attend and host events, and offer advice, careers support and opportunities.
In 2025, 48 different universities, businesses and employers visited CLC to provide advice on career routes, gap year opportunities or Higher Education options.
In 2025, students secured 120 places at Oxbridge, Russell Group and Ivy League universities. UK places included UCL, LSE, Durham, Imperial, Cambridge, Oxford, and Bath.
In 2025, students received 421 offers from top US Colleges, including Brown, Columbia, Cornell, Duke, Georgetown, Harvard, Johns Hopkins, MIT, NYU, Northwestern, Princeton and UPenn.
Our strong alumnae network spans more than 70 different countries worldwide, offering everything from university, travel and relocation advice, to a shared global outlook.
Our alumnae join Guild, a strong and active network of over 8,500 former pupils, who regularly provide expertise, advice, and opportunities.
Below, you can explore stories and successes from across our alumnae community, from personal and professional journeys to inspiring achievements.
Learn about our Guild members' diverse career pathways and the impact they continue to make in their respective fields.
